articles.title: Marquez wins in Japan to cut Martin's MotoGP lead
articles.summary: Defending MotoGP champion Marc Marquez wins a sprint-race double at the Japanese Grand Prix to cut Jorge Martin's championship lead to two points.
body: Reigning MotoGP champion Marc Marquez took maximum points at the Japanese Grand Prix, winning Saturday's sprint and Sunday's race, to cut fellow Spaniard Jorge Martin's championship lead to just two points.
Martin, 28, who won the title in 2024, finished second after starting Sunday's race at Motegi Circuit in pole position, while his Aprilla team-mate Marco Bezzecchi was third.
Ducati rider Marquez, 33, had to bide his time after Martin held his advantage off the line, but the seven-time champion took his chance on the 11th lap to edge past his rival on the inside.
"The race was tough, especially when I was behind Jorge, but I knew that if I was able to lead the race, my pace was good," said Marquez, who moved to 331 points with six rounds remaining.

articles.title: Aryna Sabalenka swept out of China Open in straight-sets defeat by Nikola Bartunkova
articles.summary: Second seed loses to 34th-ranked player from Czechia. Top seed Elena Rybakina also lost in Beijing. Aryna Sabalenka was swatted aside in straight sets by 34th-ranked Nikola Bartunkova in the third round of the China Open on Sunday, leaving the event without its top two seeds.
body: Czech player Bartunkova, 20, sent down four aces to beat the former world number one 6-4, 6-3 in one hour and 35 minutes. “I focused on myself, to be calm,” Bartunkova said. “She’s a legend … so I’m really happy that I won the match,” she said of the four-time Grand Slam champion. Bartunkova next faces Austria’s Sinja Kraus in the round of 16.
Second-seeded Sabalenka squandered five chances to break serve in the sixth game of the first set, with Bartunkova strong on defence and firing deep.
The 28-year-old from Belarus threw on a cap for the eighth game of the first set as the women switched between playing in the shade and the sun, but it did not turn the tide in her favour.

A frustrated Sabalenka tossed her racquet at a break down in the fourth game of the second set, and lost on the first match point when she returned into the net. Top seed Elena Rybakina – who weeks earlier replaced Sabalenka as World No 1 – was ousted by Alina Charaeva in the second round on Saturday.

articles.title: Sabalenka stunned by Bartunkova at China Open
articles.summary: World number two Aryna Sabalenka follows Elena Rybakina out the door at the China Open as she falls to a surprise defeat by Nikola Bartunkova.
body: World number two Aryna Sabalenka followed Elena Rybakina out the door at the China Open as she fell to a surprise defeat by 34th-ranked Nikola Bartunkova.

It comes a day after top seed Rybakina, who defeated Sabalenka in last month's US Open final and replaced the Belarusian at the top of the rankings, was knocked out by Armenian world number 118 Alina Charaeva.
Czech Bartunkova sprung another upset at the WTA 1000 tournament and continued her breakthrough season with a 6-4 6-3 over Sabalenka.
"I focused on myself, to be calm," said Bartunkova, who will face Austria's Sinja Kraus next.

articles.title: I clawed my way to the top but need a break - Azpilicueta
articles.summary: Cesar Azpilicueta says it is time to move to "a different stage of life" following a glorious 20-year playing career, notably captaining Chelsea to several titles.
body: Cesar Azpilicueta was an all-encompassing leader for Chelsea - and, now retired, he reflects on how his passion for education and attention to detail helped him build a career at the highest level.
One story sums it up. Before Chelsea 's Champions League final victory in 2021, Azpilicueta could not take his customary pre-match nap and opted to study instead.
He says his work towards an MBA in business management from the Berlin School of Business and Innovation took his mind off the pressure and noise on the streets of Porto.
Later that day, he lifted the Champions League trophy after captaining Chelsea to victory against Manchester City.

articles.title: Guardians' offensive issues show up in ALDS Game 1 vs White Sox
articles.summary: The Guardians did well during the regular season to end the year on an offensive high note, easing some concerns. But in Game 1, they returned.
body: CLEVELAND — The No. 1 concern for the Guardians through most of the summer saw its shadow again on Oct. 3. And, quickly, combatting that problem is suddenly the biggest obstacle between a trip to the ALCS or an early exit from the 2026 playoffs.
The Guardians lost 3-0 to the White Sox in Game 1 of the ALDS at Progressive Field. Game 2, now even more paramount for Cleveland, is set for 5 p.m. Monday, Oct. 5.
The Guardians have until then to figure out how to counter the White Sox’s chaotic pitching plan built on shorter starts, openers, and/or a whole lot of pitchers being thrown at them.
Chicago improved to 3-0 in the postseason, largely because of a strategy built on a high volume of pitchers entering and exiting games, never allowing opposing lineups to get comfortable.

articles.title: Daryz seeks historic Arc double
articles.summary: Daryz seeks to retain his Prix de l'Arc de Triomphe crown in the 2026 renewal of Europe's richest race - live on Sky Sports Racing at 3.05pm.
body: Daryz - last year's Prix de l'Arc de Triomphe winner - looks to become the first colt to retain the prize since 1978 when he goes to post for Europe's premier race at 3.05pm, live on Sky Sports Racing; The race is the feature of eight from Paris, alongside domestic racing from Uttoxeter.
Daryz will look for an historic back-to-back double in Europe's biggest race, bidding to be the first colt since Alleged in 1978 to achieve this feat.

Francis-Henri Graffard's colt looked as good as ever when he returned in the Prix Ganay, which was then followed up with an equally sparkling performance in the Prix Aga Khan IV. A trip to Royal Ascot in June for the Prince Of Wales' Stakes didn't go to plan as he was third, although it transpired blood issues were found following the race.

After a break, Graffard's star made light work of Coronation Cup winner Bay City Roller - who he reopposes today - in the Prix Foy, with the trainer saying he was only 75 per cent fit. Having been drawn in stall five, this short priced favourite will take all the beating with connections very confident.

articles.title: Tee Higgins Fantasy Week 4 Start or Sit: Pacing for 1,383 Yards and Still Underrated
articles.summary: Jacksonville comes to Cincinnati with Higgins 11th among wide receivers in PFN’s Week 4 rankings, and he is pacing for 1,383 receiving yards without anyone making much noise about it.
body: For those unaware, Higgins is pacing for 1,383 receiving yards this season.

The best part? I don’t see why it doesn’t stick. His PPR points per target (1.93) are nearly identical with his career rate in Joe Burrow starts (1.96), and it’s not as if he is producing in a world where Ja’Marr Chase is struggling to get his.

Higgins’ target rate, depth of target and yards per route are all moving in a very positive direction, and it’s almost like no one cares. He was one of the more undiscussed high-end players this summer, and everyone still just remains content with what he is.

That’s fine, but that sort of attitude does often impact how managers feel about moving on from a player. My guess is that you can catch the eye of the Higgins manager with a shiny toy (maybe a Jalen Coker type or Dalton Kincaid in a cross-positional setup) and make a package deal that has you gaining long-term win equity.

articles.title: Humphries to face Price in World Grand Prix final in 2023 repeat
articles.summary: Gerwyn Price and Luke Humphries will look for their second World Grand Prix titles when they meet in Sunday's final of the double-start event in Leicester.
body: Price, the 2020 champion, beat Nathan Aspinall 5-2 in Saturday's first semi-final before 2023 winner Luke Humphries defeated James Wade 5-3 to reach his fourth straight final and set up a repeat of the showpiece game three years ago - when he saw off Price 5-2.

A major drought will end either way at the Mattioli Arena, with Humphries going over a year since his last premier title - the 2025 Premier League - and Price's previous elite silverware coming way back in 2022 at the World Series of Darts Finals in Amsterdam.
Price romped into a 3-0 lead over Aspinall, peeling off two 13-darters and then a 15-darter to sweep the opener before he broke The Asp in the deciding leg of set two.
The third set went on throw until the fourth leg, when Aspinall missed six darts to hold, including two at double one, and Price subsequently pinned D10 to move 3-0 up.

articles.title: Third time lucky for Pocognoli as Scotland mark Robertson's 100th cap with win
articles.summary: Sebastien Pocognoli secured his first Scotland win at the third time of asking as captain Andy Robertson became just the second player to reach 100 caps.
body: The head coach insisted there was no extra pressure after drawing a blank in their opening two Nations League games, but he and the players silenced some critics with a strong performance in Skopje despite a second red card inside a week as they beat North Macedonia 2-0.

Robertson missed two brilliant chances before Kieron Bowie - hooked after Jack Hendry's early sending off against Switzerland in midweek - smashed the ball into the bottom corner to earn his first international goal and Scotland's first in over 420 minutes.
Play was stopped by a dog running onto the pitch before Scotland continued to dominate with Bowie, Robertson and Ben Gannon-Doak going close before the break.
Scotland were awarded a penalty when Gannon-Doak went down in the box after half-time, only for the referee to overturn his decision after being called to the monitor.
